guide.description: An introduction to EndNote Desktop for new users. Learn how to create a Library, add and modify references, use EndNote with Microsoft Word, add groups, add full-text PDFs, and back-up your EndNote Desktop library. Also includes EndNote Online

box.name: EndNote: A Beginner's Guide Quick Links

asset.description:
This guide is intended to introduce EndNote Online and EndNote Desktop to new users. Core concepts include: setting up an EndNote Online account, installing EndNote Desktop, populating your EndNote library with references, adding PDFs, inserting citations with Cite While You Write, and troubleshooting frequent issues.

EndNote in Action: How to use EndNote in 7 minutes

(NOTE: this video demonstrates EndNote 20. EndNote 21 and EndNote 2025 will look and function the same way)

EndNote is a citation management software program designed to assist with formatting citations, so you can focus on your research. The University of Tennessee maintains a campus-wide annual subscription for EndNote and it is available at no cost to students, staff, and faculty. Below are descriptions of the two types of EndNote software as well as some helpful tools for using EndNote.

The desktop version of EndNote helps you store and organize your research, download new references from library databases, create bibliographies using over 5,000 styles, use your references as you write, share with colleagues, and access and manage your research from anywhere by syncing with your EndNote online account. EndNote may be installed on a maximum of three machines per license.

Installing EndNote Desktop

  • Your UTC password must be up to date. If you have not changed your password recently, visit https://ds.utk.edu/passwords and follow the steps to reset it (existing users)
  • Visit the UTK Software Distribution site. Log in using your UTCID and password.
  • Choose Clarivate Analytics (EndNote). Choose EndNote for either Windows or Mac and click Download selected item
  • The software and instructions will download as a zipped file on your computer
  • You MUST extract (unzip) the files before you can install EndNote.
  • Once EndNote is successfully installed, you can use the sync button to connect your desktop version to your EndNote Online account if you have one (highly recommended).

EndNote online is a limited online-only version of EndNote and is perfect when you're new to research and writing. When you find yourself in need of more robust capabilities, move up to the desktop version of EndNote.

While not required in order to use EndNote Desktop, an EndNote Online account offers the important ability to sync your EndNote library to the cloud. By connecting an EndNote Online account to your EndNote Desktop, your library of references is safely backed-up to the cloud and can quickly be accessed from any computer. Note: while EndNote Online can be accessed from anywhere, you are only allowed to install EndNote Desktop on a maximum of three machines.
Next: Adding References to your EndNote Library

page.name: Adding references to your EndNote Library

box.name: EndNote: A Beginner's Guide Quick Links

asset.description:
At the core of EndNote Desktop is your Library: the file on your computer that stores all of your references. Since references can come from myriad places, including databases, journal pages, Google Scholar, the web, books, newspapers, and more, there are several ways to add references to your Library. The short video below covers the basics. Detailed instructions for Google Scholar, library databases, and manual entry follow.

EndNote in Action: Adding references

To export references from Google Scholar to EndNote Desktop:

1. Open EndNote Desktop

 

2. Navigate to Google Scholar (scholar.google.com)

Tip: Use the UTC Library's link to Google Scholar for access to articles using the Get It @ UTC link

 

3. Search for the scholarly source you want to export to EndNote.

 

4. Click the "Cite" link underneath the source you want to export to EndNote. 

 

5. Select the option to download an EndNote import file.

 

6. Once the file is saved, double-click on it to open it into EndNote Desktop. 

 

IMPORTANT:

You will often need to make slight edits to your imported reference. See the section on manually entering references for more information. In the meantime, common edits include the following:

  • Verify that the reference type is correct (i.e., book, journal article, web page, etc.)
  • Make sure authors are listed Lastname, Firstname
  • For works with more than one author, enter each author on a separate line (i.e., press Enter after each author)
  • Make sure titles are in sentence case ("Learning from words: testimony as a source of knowledge" NOT "Learning From Words: Testimony As A Source of Knowledge")
  • Verify that all of the necessary data has been imported (e.g., for a journal article: Author(s), Year, Article Title, Journal Title, Volume, Issue, Page(s))

box.name: Adding references from a library database

asset.description:
To export references from a library database into your EndNote Desktop library:

1. Open EndNote.

2. Go to a library database of your choice and search for you topic.

3. Mark or select the references from your search results that you would like to export into your EndNote Desktop library.

4. Different databases will have different names for the EndNote export function, including Cite; Export; Send to; EndNote; and Save 

5. Look for the option to download either an EndNote or RIS file. Download the file to your computer, double-click on it, and it should open directly into EndNote Desktop.

IMPORTANT:

You will often need to make slight edits to your imported reference. See the section on manually entering references for more information. In the meantime, common edits include the following:

  • Verify that the reference type is correct (i.e., book, article, web page, etc.)
  • Make sure authors are listed Lastname, Firstname
  • For works with more than one author, enter each author on a separate line (i.e., press Enter after each author)
  • Make sure titles are in sentence case ("Learning from words: testimony as a source of knowledge" NOT "Learning From Words: Testimony As A Source of Knowledge")
  • Verify that all of the necessary data has been imported (e.g., for a journal article: Author(s), Year, Article Title, Journal Title, Volume, Issue, Page(s))

References can be manually created in an EndNote Desktop. Examples of a reference requiring manual creation would be a report from a government department's website, information or images from other websites, artwork from a gallery or museum, podcasts, YouTube videos, social media posts, company or industry reports, and unpublished works.

To manually create a reference in your EndNote Desktop library:

1. Create a new reference: References > New Reference OR click on the right of the toolbar towards the top.

 

2. The default setting for new references is Journal Article . If you are using something else, you can change the reference type within the Reference Type drop-down list, e.g. Book, Book Section [for book chapters in edited books], Conference Paper, Web Page, etc.

3. Fill in the content for the fields you need. Then, File > Save or press Save button on the top right corner . Click the white/blue cross  to close the reference.

4. The reference has now been manually created.

IMPORTANT:

EndNote has specific criteria for how you must enter bibliographic information. Key things to note:

  • Verify that the reference type is correct (i.e., book, journal article, web page, etc.)
  • Make sure authors are listed Lastname, Firstname
  • For works with more than one author, enter each author on a separate line (i.e., press Enter after each author)
  • Make sure titles are in sentence case ("Learning from words: testimony as a source of knowledge" NOT "Learning From Words: Testimony As A Source of Knowledge")
  • Verify that all of the necessary data has been imported (e.g., for a journal article: Author(s), Year, Article Title, Journal Title, Volume, Issue, Page(s))

Adding PDFs to your references

  • EndNote allows you to attach PDFs to each reference. 
  • Open your desired reference and look for the tab that says PDF
Next: Editing References

box.name: EndNote: A Beginner's Guide Quick Links

asset.description:
Required fields

In order for EndNote to generate proper citations, each reference type has certain minimum requirements. For the most common source types, these include:

 

 

Journal Article

  • Author(s)
  • Year
  • Title
  • Journal Name
  • Volume
  • Issue Pages

Book

  • Author(s)
  • Year
  • Title
  • Place Published
  • Publisher

Book Section (i.e., a book chapter)

  • Author(s)
  • Year
  • Title
  • Place Published
  • Publisher
  • Pages

Web Page

  • Author(s)
  • Year
  • Title
  • URL
  • Access Date

(Note: Scroll down to find the URL field.)

Works by a single author

  • List author names with last name first. (e.g., Smith, Patti)

Works by two or more authors

  • List each author with their last name first. (e.g., Smith, Patti)
  • Enter each author on a separate line (i.e., press 'Enter' after each author)

Organization and Corporate Authors

  • When the author is an organization, enter the name in full, followed by a comma.
  • Failure to include a comma makes EndNote interpret the organization as a personal name in your citations. (e.g., The University of Tennessee at Chattanooga would become "Chattanooga, T.U.o.C.")

Editing titles

  • Titles must be entered in sentence case.

Editing journal names

  • Enter journal names in sentence case. 
  • See the EndNote support page if you need to customize journal names.

Editing publisher names

  • Enter the full name of the publisher, without abbreviation. (EndNote will abbreviate for you, depending on your citation style.)
Next: EndNote and Microsoft Word

page.name: MS Word and Cite While You Write

asset.description: Please select your operating system.

The best option for dealing with EndNote issues is to contact the UTC Library. Your librarians can answer questions via email, chat, or one-on-one consultations (either in-person or online).

Click here to make an appointment. 

Click here to email us your question at library@utc.edu.

Answers to the following common questions can be found below:

EndNote Desktop

  • Can I use EndNote with a cloud drive (like OneDrive or Google Drive)?
  • How do I use EndNote on multiple computers?

Cite While You Write

  • My bibliography is gone and in-text citations are appearing as {Reed 1967 #431}
  • Author names not correct in my in-text citations or bibliography.
  • Journal and/or book titles are not formatted correctly.
  • My bibliography is formatted incorrectly (i.e., wrong font, wrong indentation, wrong spacing, etc.)

Can I use EndNote Desktop with a cloud folder, like Google Drive or OneDrive?

Do not save your EndNote library in a cloud folder, this can permanently corrupt your library.

You can save your Word documents in the cloud and still use Cite While You Write; Cite While You Write does not work with Google Docs or the online version of Word.

 

Can I use EndNote on multiple computers?

If you want to use EndNote Desktop on multiple computers, you will want to sync EndNote Desktop to your EndNote Online account. 

1. In EndNote Desktop, go to Edit > Preferences

2. Select the option to Sync.

3. Select Enable Sync and enter your EndNote online credentials. Click here if you need to create an EndNote Online account or if you forgot your password. Click Apply and then OK.

Make sure that each computer syncs to your online account. Now, each time you open EndNote Desktop, it will sync all changes. You can also click the Sync Configuration link at the top of the left-hand column in EndNote at any time to sync.

My bibliography is gone and in-text citations are appearing as {Reed, 1967 #431}

Citations in curly brackets {} are temporary citations created because Instant Formatting is turned off. To enable, in Word > select EndNote tab > click on the arrow beside the button "Instant Formatting is Off" and choose "Turn Instant Formatting On."
 

When I edit my citations or bibliography, the edits keep reverting every time I reopen Word.

The citations you insert from EndNote are mapped to your EndNote Library. Every time you reopen Word, Cite While You Write pulls the bibliographic information from EndNote, overwriting any edits you attempted in Word.

To fix this, make sure you perform all edits to references in EndNote. To edit a citation, from the EndNote tab select Edit and Manage Citation(s).

 

Author names are formatted incorrectly.

Problem Example Correct formatting
Author first names are appearing in my in-text citations. The author John Cale displays in your text as (John 1967) instead of (Cale 1967).

Authors must be entered into EndNote with the last name first, like:

Cale, John
For a source with multiple authors, the names are jumbled and inconsistent.

For the authors John Cale, Maureen Tucker, and Sterling Morrison, your in-text citation might appear as

(John Cale 1967)

and your bibliography might appear as

John Cale, M.T., Sterling Morrison (1967)

Multiple authors must be entered into EndNote on separate lines, like
Organization names are treated as personal names

The Velvet Underground 

might appear in your citations as

Underground, T. V.

EndNote cannot distinguish between personal names and organization names. 

Organization names should have a comma at the end, like:

The Velvet Underground,

How do I reformat my bibliography?

If you want to adjust the font, line-spacing, or indentation of your bibliography, you must use the Configure Bibliography tool. On the EndNote tab, look for the small arrow next to Bibliography. This opens a new window; the Layout tab will have all the options you need to customize your bibliography.

Cite While You Write (CWYW) is an add-in for Microsoft Word that should be automatically installed when you install EndNote Desktop. You should see a tab in Word that indicates CWYW has been installed.

See the troubleshooting section if Cite While You Write does not appear in Word.

To insert a citation into your paper, follow these steps:

From the EndNote tab in Word:

1. Select the style you prefer (e.g., APA, Chicago, or MLA).

2. Place your cursor at the exact location you want to insert a citation.

3. Click "Insert Citation" in the upper left of the EndNote tab.

4. A new window will pop up. Use the search bar to search for a reference in your EndNote Library (searching by last name is probably easiest).

5. Click the reference you want to insert.

6. Click "Insert"

Your citation should now be inserted and match the style you selected. Notice that the citation is highlighted in grey. This is to indicate that the citation is being pulled in from EndNote.

box.name: Cite While You Write: Editing Citations

asset.description:
By default, EndNote will only insert the author name and the year into a parenthetical citation. However, sometimes you may want your in-text citation to appear in an alternate format, such as with the author name outside the parentheses, with a page number, or with a prefix like "e.g." or "ibid."

There are two ways to customize your in-text citations:

Option 1: Edit before inserting

The first option is to edit the citation before inserting into the text. When you go to insert a citation, instead of clicking on Insert, click the small arrow just to the right of the insert button. This brings up five insert options:

  • Insert
    • This will insert as (Author, Year)
  • Insert & Display as: Author (year)
  • Insert & Exclude Author
  • Insert & Exclude Year
  • Insert in Bibliography Only

Option 2: Edit citations after inserting

The second option allows a bit more fine-tuning of citations.

1. Highlight the citation you want to edit.

2. Select Edit & Manage Citation(s) from the EndNote toolbar.

3. To change whether the author name is inside or outside of the citation, select the Formatting drop-down to get the same options as in Option 1.

4. In this example, a specific page number was added in the Pages field. You can also add a Prefix or Suffix (like e.g. or etc.)

 

EndNote In Action

box.name: Cite While You Write: Formatting Your Bibliography

asset.description:
When you insert a citation, EndNote adds a corresponding entry to a bibliography at the end of your paper. Since this bibliography is generated by EndNote, you must use EndNote's Cite While You Write tool if you need to modify things like font, spacing, or indentations.

To modify your bibliography

1. On the EndNote tab in Word, click the small arrow in the Bibliography section of the toolbar

2. Select the Layout tab in the window that pops up.

3. You should see options to set the font, font size, line spacing, and indentation.
Next: Troubleshooting EndNote issues

Cite While You Write (CWYW) is an add-in for Microsoft Word that should be automatically installed when you install EndNote Desktop. You should see a tab in Word that indicates CWYW has been installed.

6. Click "Insert"

guide.name: Introduction to the Library Studio Equipment
guide.description: If you're thinking about making a film, podcast, or the next award-winning song but don't know what kind of equipment you need, this guide can help! This guide will break down the types of equipment the Studio has to offer to help you create your next mas

asset.description:
What is the Studio?

The UTC Library Studio (3rd Floor) is a workspace for innovative technology and media creation. Produce a documentary, prototype your invention with 3D modeling or graphic software, digitize that old box of slides, and everything in between. We have 24 workstations loaded with specialized software, audio, and video equipment that can be checked out for class and personal use, and dedicated spaces to make your dream projects a reality. We also have faculty and staff to help you get started, regardless of your experience level.

box.name: How to Check Out Studio Equipment

asset.description:
The Library Studio has both first-come, first-served and reserved equipment. Equipment typically checks out for 3-days at a time, but some pieces, such as the synths and midis, may have a longer checkout period.

First-Come, First-Served Equipment

First-come, first-served equipment is non-reservable equipment you can pick up anytime during our open hours. As these are first-come, first-served with limited availability, we recommend calling ahead to ensure it is currently available.

Reserved Equipment

For those who prefer to plan ahead, we also offer equipment that can be reserved through the Studio's website. If you need help making a reservation, you can call the Studio service desk or come in to ask for help. If you want to make a reservation for one of the suites, you can watch this video on how to reserve Studio equipment or this video explaining how to reserve our Studio Video or Audio Suite. 

When you're ready to pick up your reservation, simply come to the Studio's service desk (Library 305) and tell us that you are picking up some equipment. Be sure to bring your Mocs ID, the GET mobile app, or some other physical, government-issued identification. We cannot accept photos of your ID on your phone or computer. Also, if you do not pick up the equipment on the first day of your reservation period, your reservation will be deleted when the Studio closes.

If you're looking for something specific, click one of the links below to jump directly to that type of equipment.

  • Audio Interfaces and Guitar Pedals
  • Audio Recording Equipment
  • Cameras
  • Camera Accessories & Tripods
  • Event & Presentation Equipment
  • Lighting and Backgrounds
  • Music Production Equipment

Audio Interface

This audio interface has two XLR inputs to record vocals or instruments directly into audio editing software. Because of the two inputs, it allows for simultaneous recording. This item is not available to reserve in advance. Please ask if it is available at the Studio service desk.

Guitar Pedal: Mood MKII

The Mood MKII is a two-channel multi-effect pedal. One half samples and loops and the other is a suite of real-time spatial effects. The two channels are aware of each other and work together. You can process the micro-loops with the spatial effects or record those effects into the loops. This item is not available to reserve in advance. Please ask if it is available at the Studio service desk.

Guitar Pedal: Strymon Big Sky

The Strymon Big Sky reverb pedal is MIDI-compatible and comes with 300 built-in presets. This item is not available to reserve in advance. Please ask if it is available at the Studio service desk.

Guitar Pedal: Strymon Iridium

The Strymon Iridium is an amp & IR Cab pedal with three different amp types, each with three different speaker cabinet options that compliment the tonality of the amp. Includes: Three Iconic Amplifiers, Nine Stereo IR Cabinets, and Adjustable Room Ambience settings. This item is not available to reserve in advance. Please ask if it is available at the Studio service desk.

Guitar Pedal: Strymon Timeline

The Strymon Timeline delay pedal is MIDI-compatible and comes with 200 built-in presets. This item is not available to reserve in advance. Please ask if it is available at the Studio service desk.

Blue Yeti Mic

The Yeti is a desktop USB mic that simply needs to be plugged into your computer to use. It's perfect if you have a quiet room set up and just want to talk into a mic. You can either reserve one ahead of time or just come to the Studio desk and ask for one.

Condenser Mics

These are perfect if you have a little more experience, and are looking for that something special. You can either reserve one ahead of time or just come to the Studio desk and ask for one. The Rode Condenser mic has an XLR output, so you willneed an audio interface, Zoom H6, or Rodecaster to use it.

Rodecaster Pro

An audio interface and microphone designed specifically for Podcasting. The interface includes 4 mic preamps, 8 faders, 8 programmable pads, USB to Host connection, and Bluetooth capability. You can reserve one here.

Zoom H1

The Zoom H1 is a one-button, portable recorder that's great for interviews on the go. It can also be used as a USB mic if one of the Yetis isn't available. And, yes, it comes with that nifty tripod. You can't make a reservation for an H1. Just come and ask at the desk.

Zoom H6

The Zoom H6 is the H1's big sibling. It comes with three interchangeable mic capsules (omnidirectional, mid-side, and shotgun), but it has extra ports you can connect XLR or 1/4" cables to. It's great for capturing interviews on the go or recording your band in your living room. You can reserve one here.

Cinema Camera (Panasonic GH7)

The Cinema camera is a specialty camera that can create a more "cinematic" effect. If you've ever watched a scene where the camera focuses between two characters (one close to the camera and one far away), you can achieve that effect with this camera. This camera has both auto and manual focus, and it can shoot in HD and 4K. You can reserve one here or give us a call to see if we have our first-come, first-served kit available.

Compact Camera (Lumix G100D)

The Compact Camera is the perfect camera if you are looking for something lightweight, that can take both photos and videos or if you want to learn the basics of manual photography without the intimidation of the advanced settings that a typical DSLR has. This camera can shoot in HD and 4K. You can either reserve one ahead of time or just come to the Studio desk and ask for one.

DJI Osmo Pocket

Like the GoPro, the Osmo is best suited for filming videos that involve movement. The Osmo is positioned on its own gimbal, which helps stabilize your video as you move around. This camera can shoot in HD and 4K. You can reserve one here or ask for one at the Studio's service desk.

GoPro Hero 9

The GoPro Kit is our recommendation if you want to capture action shots. This kit comes with a media mod to capture higher-quality audio, a waterproof case (you will have to remove the media mod for this), and a hand-held tripod. If you want a hands-free recording experience, chest mounts and head mounts are also available upon request. This camera can shoot in HD and 4K. You can reserve one here or ask for one at the Studio's service desk.

Hybrid Camera (Lumix GH6)

The Hybrid camera is a great multi-functional camera that allows the user to take various photos and videos with interchangeable lenses in both automatic and manual modes. This kit comes with two lenses, but more are available upon request.  This camera can shoot in HD and 4K. You can either reserve one ahead of time or just come to the Studio desk and ask for one.

Insta360 X3

The Insta360 X3 is a 360-degree camera that can be used to take your videography to a new level. You cannot reserve these camera kits in advance. Instead, you will need to come to the Studio desk and ask for one.

* This kit comes with a selfie stick, but tripods are available upon request.

** Insta360 Studio is needed to edit the footage from this camera. The software is available in the Studio.

Mini HD Camera

The Mini HD camera is great for beginners who want to explore videography without jumping straight into our larger, more complicated kits. This camera shoots in HD, not 4K. You cannot reserve these camera kits in advance. Instead, you will need to come to the Studio desk and ask for one.

UHD Camera (Canon XA-60)

The UHD camera is a step above the Mini HD in size and complexity. This kit comes with an external microphone and many more features to help you get the audio and video quality you want. This camera shoots in HD, UHD, and 4K. You can either reserve one ahead of time or just come to the Studio desk and ask for one.

Accessory Camera Lenses

Specialty lenses are available for our Cinema Camera, Compact Camera, and Hybrid Camera kits. For a full list of the lenses, please visit the Camera Accessories page on the Studio's website. The lenses cannot be reserved in advance. Please call or drop by the Studio to ask if the lens you want is available.

DJI Osmo Mobile 6

This item is perfect if you want to film using your phone without worrying too much about shakey video, this is what we recommend. This kit requires the DJI app to use. This item is first-come, first-served and cannot be reserved in advance. Please call or come to the Studio's service desk to ask if it is available.

External Video Microphone

If you want to boost the audio quality of your video on the Mini HD or Hybrid Camera, this is the microphone for you! Simply attach the microphone to a shoe mount for the Mini HD or the top of a Hybrid Camera and insert the microphone's cable into the camera's mic input to begin picking up sound. You can't make a reservation for this item. Just come to the Studio service desk and ask.

Mobile Phone Tripod Attachment

If you want to use your phone to record a video and need something simple to keep it in place, we recommend checking out this mobile phone attachment with one of our standard or tabletop tripods. This attachment has a grip that can swivel to allow filming in both portrait and landscape mode. We have two sizes: one for smaller phone models and one for larger phones.

This item cannot be reserved ahead of time. Please come to the Studio's service desk and ask if we have one available.

Mobile Vlogging Kit

This kit is best suited for those who want to focus on vlogging. The kit comes with a tripod, phone grip, mini LED light, colored filters for the LED light, and a microphone that can attach directly to your phone (you may need to remove your phone case to allow the microphone to successfully connect). This kit is available for both iOS and Android. Please let us know what type of phone you have so we can give you the correct kit. You can reserve a kit ahead of time for an iOS device or a device with a USB-C port or just come to the Studio desk and ask for one.

Rode Wireless Go II

The Wireless Go mics are great for getting action sound where you can't be across the table from your subject. They plug into any camera or phone (adapter may be needed), and also record directly into the receiver. You can reserve one here.

Ronin Gimbal

This piece of equipment is a tripod attachment. If you need a wider recording range or need to record something from a top-down view, this piece of equipment can help you with that. You can't make a reservation for this item. Just come to the Studio service desk and ask.

Tripod Arm

This piece of equipment is a tripod attachment. If you need a wider recording range or need to record something from a top-down view, this piece of equipment can help you with that. You can't make a reservation for this item. Just come to the Studio service desk and ask.

Tripods

If you want to stabilize the camera so you don't get shaky footage, make sure you check out a tripod. We have both floating and flat-head tripods. Floating-head tripods allow you to shoot in portrait and landscape modes. The flat-head tripods only allow recording in landscape mode. If you are recording video, we recommend the flat-head tripod. If you are taking photos, we recommend the floating-head tripod. You can't make a reservation for this item. Just come to the Studio service desk and ask.

Event Speaker (JBL IRX One)

This speaker is the perfect addition to your next event. It has a 6-channel mixer, an XLR and a 1/4" input, and can connect to Bluetooth devices. If you check this speaker out, we also recommend checking out a hand cart as well. Please reserve this item in advance.

FlashFish Portable Generator

If you are planning an outdoor event, a weekend trip, or have a power outage, this portable generator will save you the headache of worrying about your electronics dying. This generator comes with 2 AC 200W outlets, 2 DC 12V/10A (Max) outputs, and 3 USB ports (2 QC). You cannot reserve this item in advance. Please call or drop by the Studio to ask if we have one available.

Hand Cart

Sometimes it's difficult to carry all of the amazing equipment you just checked out from the Studio. If you need a little help, this hand cart that can hold up to 350 lbs (158 kg) will help solve that problem! Please reserve one in advance if you know you will need it. We highly recommend reserving one if you are checking out an event speaker.

Logitech Wireless Presenter

This wireless presenter is the perfect companion for presentations and workshops. It connects to your computer via a USB port, and it comes with a built-in laser pointer and slid clicker. You cannot reserve this item in advance. Please call or drop by the Studio to ask if we have one available.

Power Box

This kit comes with a power strip and a 15-foot extension cord, making it a must-have for any outdoor event. You cannot reserve this item in advance. Please call or drop by the Studio to ask if we have one available.

Projector: Large Projector

This projector is a little larger than the medium projector. If you check out this projector, we recommend checking out the large projector screen with it. You can either reserve one ahead of time or just come to the Studio desk and ask for one.

Projector: Medium-Sized Projector

This projector is great for events such as a presentation, a movie night with a large group of people, or projecting images to trace on large items such as a wall or banner. You can either reserve one ahead of time or just come to the Studio desk and ask for one.

Projector: Pico Projector

This small, lightweight projector is great for group study sessions or movie nights. These projectors are not available to be reserved in advance. Please ask us if there is one available at the Studio service desk.

Projector Screen: Large Projector Screen (Da-Lite 44" x 74")

This projector screen is recommended to be used with the Large Projector. You must reserve one ahead of time.

Projector Screen: Medium Projector Screen (Da-Lite 36" x 74")

This projector screen is recommended to be used with Medium or Large Projectors. You must reserve one ahead of time.

Wireless Microphone Kit (x2 Handheld)

This mic kit is perfect to use with the Event Speaker. It comes with two handheld microphones and a base receiver that will be connected to an audio system via an XLR cable. If you need to use both microphones, please request another XLR cable. Please reserve this kit ahead of time.

Wireless Microphone Kit (x1 Handheld, x1 Lavalier)

This mic kit is perfect to use with the Event Speaker. It comes with one handheld microphone, one lavalier microphone, and a base receiver that will be connected to an audio system via an XLR cable. If you need to use both microphones, please request another XLR cable. Please reserve this kit ahead of time.

Wireless Microphone Kit (x2 Lavalier)

This mic kit is perfect to use with the Event Speaker. It comes with two lavalier microphones and a base receiver that will be connected to an audio system via an XLR cable. If you need to use both microphones, please request another XLR cable. Please reserve this kit ahead of time.

3-Point iKan Lighting Kit

If you're looking for more advanced lighting than the ring light can provide, the 3-point iKan Light Kit may work better for your project. With this kit, you have more control over light and shadows to create the specific mood you're going for. You can either reserve one ahead of time or just come to the Studio desk and ask for one.

LED Light Stick

This LED light stick comes with 2 sides: one that has a cool to warm range and one that ranges throughout the color spectrum. It also has multiple lighting modes such as campfire, fireworks, and a mode that syncs up with sound to help create the lighting atmosphere you want. These are not available to reserve in advance. Please call or drop by the Studio to ask if one is available.

LED Camera Light Accessory

This camera light attachment can provide extra light while filming. It has manual switches to turn off, on, and change the intensity of the light. It does not flash or act as a strobe light. Please come to the Studio desk and ask if one is available.

Light Tracing Pad

This kit comes with a charging cable and carrying case.You can't make a reservation for this item. Just come to the Studio service desk and ask.

Photography Lightbox

If you want to take photos of small items such as crafting projects, your latest portfolio piece, or items for a product launch, this lightbox will help your photos look more professional. This kit comes with white, black, gray, peach, and light blue backgrounds. This kit is not available to reserve in advance. Please call or drop by the Studio to ask if one is available.

Pop-Up Photo Background

If you're looking for a more professional background for professional headshots or product photos, our pop-up photo background can help! This photo background is black on one side and white on the other. You can either reserve one ahead of time or just come to the Studio desk and ask for one.

Portable Green Screen

Whether you want a background for your stream or want to replace your Zoom background to make your friends believe you're on a relaxing trip at the beach, our portable green screen can help! You can either reserve one ahead of time or just come to the Studio desk and ask for one.

Ring Light

If you're looking for lighting that is simple to use, give the ring light a try! This item has the ability to cast both cool and warm light on whatever you're filming. You can either reserve one ahead of time or just come to the Studio desk and ask for one.

Studio in a Box

If you're not quite sure what you want to do or you want multiple backgrounds for your grand idea, check out the Studio in a Box. This kit comes with a black/white pop-up background, a pop-up green screen, and a ring light. Make sure you reserve this kit in advance as we only have one kit available.

Audio Mixer: Zoom R20

The Zoom R20 is a 16-track multitrack recorder, editor, and mixing workstation with an LCD touchscreen and 8 XLR channels with 2 housing line inputs. It is MIDI-connectable and includes 150 built-in rhythm patterns. You cannot reserve this item in advance. Please call or drop by the Studio to ask if it is available.

Midi Controller: Akai MPK25

The Akai MPK25 is a 25-key, 12-pad, 12-knob USB MIDI keyboard controller. This item is plug-and-play via its included USB cable. Midi Controllers are not able to be reserved ahead of time. You must ask if they are available at the Studio service desk.

Midi Controller: APC40

The APC40 includes a 40-pad clip-launch matrix with RGB feedback for clip status, color coding, and more. It has 8 channel faders, 1 master fader, and 8 device controls to map directly to Ableton Live. Midi Controllers are not able to be reserved ahead of time. You must as if they are available at the Studio service desk.

Midi Controller: Arturia Keystep

This easy-to-use midi controller is a 32-key keyboard that offers velocity and aftertouch controls. It has a built-in arpeggiator and sequencer. It has a vast array of connections, making it a great addition to any set-up. Midi Controllers are not able to be reserved ahead of time. You must as if they are available at the Studio service desk.

Midi Controller: Dave Smith Mopho x4

The Dave Smith Mopho x4 is a large analog synthesizer with MIDI functionality. It has 44 semi-weighted keys with an aftertouch. It also contains four voices, each with two analog oscillators and two sub-octave generators. Each voice has three 5-stage envelope generators and four LFOs. Midi Controllers cannot be reserved ahead of time. You must ask if they are available at the Studio service desk.

Synthesizer: Arturia Drumbrute

The Arturia Drumbrute is an analog drum machine with 17 drum sounds. It stores up to 64 patterns (up to 64 steps each), and it has 12 individual audio outputs to make it easy to record your patterns as multitrack audio. This item is not available to reserve in advance. Please ask if it is available at the Studio service desk.

Synthesizer: Arturia Microbrute

The Arturia Microbrute is a 3-waveform voltage-controlled oscillator with Saw, Triangle, and Square waves. It is a simple, yet powerful sequencer. Midi Controllers are not able to be reserved ahead of time. You must ask if they are available at the Studio service desk.

Synthesizer: Arturia Microfreak

The Arturia Microfreak is a hybrid synthesizer with 128 built-in sound presents, a digital oscillator with variable mode, an analog state variable filter, LFO,  Envelope and Cycling Envelope, a 25-note PCB "keyboard," Transpose buttons, Arpeggiator/Sequencer, Assignable Mod Matrix, OLED Screen, CV/Gate connection, and PSU & USB Power. This item is not available to reserve in advance. Please ask if it is available at the Studio service desk.

Synthesizer: Korg Minilogue

The Korg Minilogue is a powerful four-voice synthesizer with an oscilloscope function that shows the waveform visually. It also features an arpeggiator and a 16-step sequencer. This item is not available to reserve in advance. Please ask if it is available at the Studio service desk.

Synthesizers: Roland TR-09 and TB-03

These are a compact re-creation of Roland's classic step-based synthesizers. They are highly portable and include a built-in speaker. This item is not available to reserve in advance. Please ask if it is available at the Studio service desk.

box.name: Find On the Shelf: New Arrivals

asset.name: The Elephant in the Brain: Hidden motives in every day life
asset.description: Human beings are primates, and primates are political animals. Our brains, therefore, are designed not just to hunt and gather, but also to help us get ahead socially, often via deception and self-deception. But while we may be self-interested schemers, we benefit by pretending otherwise. Theless we know about our own ugly motives, the better - and thus we don't like to talk or even think about the extent of our selfishness. This is "the elephant in the brain." Such an introspective taboo makes it hard for us to think clearly about our nature and the explanations for our behavior. Theaim of this book, then, is to confront our hidden motives directly - to track down the darker, unexamined corners of our psyches and blast them with floodlights. Then, once everything is clearly visible, we can work to better understand ourselves: Why do we laugh? Why are artists sexy? Why do webrag about travel? Why do we prefer to speak rather than listen?Our unconscious motives drive more than just our private behavior; they also infect our venerated social institutions such as Art, School, Charity, Medicine, Politics, and Religion. In fact, these institutions are in many ways designed to accommodate our hidden motives, to serve covert agendasalongside their "official" ones. The existence of big hidden motives can upend the usual political debates, leading one to question the legitimacy of these social institutions, and of standard policies designed to favor or discourage them. You won't see yourself - or the world - the same afterconfronting the elephant in the brain.
asset.author: Kevin Simler; Robin Hanson

asset.name: Reader, Come Home: The reading brain in a digital world
asset.description: From the author of Proust and the Squid, a lively, ambitious, and deeply informative epistolary book that considers the future of the reading brain and our capacity for critical thinking, empathy, and reflection as we become increasingly dependent on digital technologies. A decade ago, Maryanne Wolf's Proust and the Squid revealed what we know about how the brain learns to read and how reading changes the way we think and feel. Since then, the ways we process written language have changed dramatically with many concerned about both their own changes and that of children. New research on the reading brain chronicles these changes in the brains of children and adults as they learn to read while immersed in a digitally dominated medium. Drawing deeply on this research, this book comprises a series of letters Wolf writes to us--her beloved readers--to describe her concerns and her hopes about what is happening to the reading brain as it unavoidably changes to adapt to digital mediums. Wolf raises difficult questions, including: Will children learn to incorporate the full range of "deep reading" processes that are at the core of the expert reading brain? Will the mix of a seemingly infinite set of distractions for children's attention and their quick access to immediate, voluminous information alter their ability to think for themselves? With information at their fingertips, will the next generation learn to build their own storehouse of knowledge, which could impede the ability to make analogies and draw inferences from what they know? Will all these influences, in turn, change the formation in children and the use in adults of "slower" cognitive processes like critical thinking, personal reflection, imagination, and empathy that comprise deep reading and that influence both how we think and how we live our lives? Will the chain of digital influences ultimately influence the use of the critical analytical and empathic capacities necessary for a democratic society? How can we preserve deep reading processes in future iterations of the reading brain? Who are the "good readers" of every epoch? Concerns about attention span, critical reasoning, and over-reliance on technology are never just about children--Wolf herself has found that, though she is a reading expert, her ability to read deeply has been impacted as she has become, inevitably, increasingly dependent on screens. Wolf draws on neuroscience, literature, education, technology, and philosophy and blends historical, literary, and scientific facts with down-to-earth examples and warm anecdotes to illuminate complex ideas that culminate in a proposal for a biliterate reading brain. Provocative and intriguing, Reader, Come Home is a roadmap that provides a cautionary but hopeful perspective on the impact of technology on our brains and our most essential intellectual capacities--and what this could mean for our future.
asset.author: Maryanne Wolf

asset.name: Toxic Geek Masculinity in Media: sexism, trolling, and identity policing
asset.description: This book examines changing representations of masculinity in geek media, during a time of transition in which "geek" has not only gone mainstream but also become a more contested space than ever, with continual clashes such as Gamergate, the Rabid and Sad Puppies' attacks on the Hugo Awards, and battles at conventions over "fake geek girls." Anastasia Salter and Bridget Blodgett critique both gendered depictions of geeks, including shows like Chuck and The Big Bang Theory, and aspirational geek heroes, ranging from the Winchester brothers of Supernatural to BBC's Sherlock and the varied superheroes of the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Through this analysis, the authors argue that toxic masculinity is deeply embedded in geek culture, and that the identity of geek as victimized other must be redefined before geek culture and media can ever become an inclusive space.
asset.author: Anastasia Salter; Bridget Blodgett

asset.name: Therapy with a Coaching Edge
asset.description: In Therapy with a Coaching Edge, professional practice guru Lynn Grodzki offers a new, paradigm-changing therapy model--adding the leverage and action of a coaching approach to the wisdom and goals of psychotherapy. This book presents a set of powerful coaching strategies that have been adapted and designed specifically for therapy--to provide more reach and range for therapists and counselors while not requiring a wholesale abandonment of therapeutic principles. Using this model, therapists at all levels of experience can promote behavioral change without insisting on homework or rigid protocols. Clients can spot results in each and every therapy session. Resistance to treatment often softens and client retention improves.  Grodzki gives new and veteran clinicians the skills to not only improve client outcomes, but also energize themselves as practitioners. Therapists feel empowered as they learn to ask compelling questions that generate "ah-ha" moments. They help clients go beyond a discussion of symptoms to explore topics of core values. They show clients how to make decisions based on both necessity and a vision of a better future. The model provides readers with just-in-time learning, to identify a skill when it is needed an then immediately apply the steps in a session. Grodzki, an expert psychotherapist and master certified coach, has proven herself to be a trusted voice for therapists through her writing and workshops; she makes the steps to using a coaching approach understandable by offering lively case examples, "your turn" exercises, and sample scripts to give her readers the confidence and context to move forward.
asset.author: Lynn Grodzki

asset.name: The Influential Mind: What the Brain Reveals About Our Power to Change Others‎
asset.description: A cutting-edge, research-based inquiry into how we influence those around us and how understanding the brain can help us change minds for the better. InThe Influential Mind, neuroscientist Tali Sharot takes us on a thrilling exploration of the nature of influence. We all have a duty to affect others--from the classroom to the boardroom to social media. But how skilled are we at this role, and can we become better? It turns out that many of our instincts--from relying on facts and figures to shape opinions, to insisting others are wrong or attempting to exert control--are ineffective, because they are incompatible with how people's minds operate. Sharot shows us how to avoid these pitfalls, and how an attempt to change beliefs and actions is successful when it is well-matched with the core elements that govern the human brain. Sharot reveals the critical role of emotion in influence, the weakness of data and the power of curiosity. Relying on the latest research in neuroscience, behavioral economics and psychology, the book provides fascinating insight into the complex power of influence, good and bad.
asset.author: Tali Sharot

asset.name: Encyclopedia of Educational Psychology
asset.description: The field of educational psychology draws from a variety of diverse disciplines including human development across the life span, measurement and statistics, learning and motivation, and teaching. And within these different disciplines, many other fields are featured including psychology, anthropology, education, sociology, public health, school psychology, counseling, history, and philosophy. In fact, when taught at the college or university level, educational psychology is an ambitious course that undertakes the presentation of many different topics all tied together by the theme of how the individual can best function in an "educational" setting, loosely defined as anything from pre-school through adult education. Educational psychology can be defined as the application of what we know about learning and motivation, development, and measurement and statistics to educational settings (both school- and community-based).
asset.author: Neil J. Salkind (Editor)

asset.name: Encyclopedia of Multicultural Psychology
asset.description: The Encyclopedia of Multicultural Psychology is the first authoritative guide to synthesize the dynamic field of multicultural psychology. This volume includes entries on a broad array of issues and covers the breadth of psychology viewed through the lens of the racial and ethnic minority experience. The Encyclopedia addresses culture across a broad spectrum of psychological perspectives and includes topics that are relevant to social psychology, cognitive psychology, environmental psychology, cross-cultural psychology, and clinical psychology.

box.name: Planning out Your Project with SAGE Research Methods

asset.description:
SAGE Research Methods can help you with every stage of your research project. 

Nearly every research project has 9 main steps:

  1. Defining a Topic
  2. Developing a Researchable Research Question
  3. Designing Your Research and Choosing Your Method
  4. Researching Ethically and Safely
  5. Reviewing the Literature
  6. Doing Fieldwork/Gathering Data
  7. Analyzing Your Data/Findings
  8. Writing Up
  9. Dissemination

1. Defining a Topic

You may already have a topic in mind, or your topic was assigned to you.  If not, search "Topic" in SAGE Research Methods. This book chapter entry will help you choose a sound area to study:

asset.name: Choosing a Topic
asset.description: Book chapter from Doing Your Undergraduate Project.

2. Developing a Researchable Research Question

A research question is more refined than a topic.  For help writing your research question, check out the SAGE resources below or start by reading an introductory article.

asset.name: SAGE Resources for Research Questions
asset.description: Resources to help develop research questions.

asset.name: Research Question Intro Article
asset.description: From the Encyclopedia of Research Design

3. Designing Your Research and Choosing Your Method

The Methods Map can help you choose a method if you’re not sure which to use.  If you already have your method, you can search directly for it.  The search results will provide both brief explanations of the method via dictionary and encyclopedia entries as well as in-depth how-tos in book-length entries.

asset.name: SAGE Research Methods Map
asset.description: Explore research methods, read definitions, and discover content.

4. Researching Ethically and Safely

If ethics is a concern for your project, SRM contains a number of resources to help.

asset.name: Research Ethics for Social Scientists
asset.description: Access online through SAGE Research Methods.

5. Reviewing the Literature

A literature review is a crucial step to monitor what has already been written about your topic. SRM has many resources on how to conduct a literature review.

asset.name: SAGE Resources for Literature Reviews
asset.description: Resources for developing literature reviews.

6. Doing Fieldwork/Gathering Data

7. Analyzing Your Data/Findings

8. Writing Up

Books with step-by-step information on hundreds of data collection methods are included.  In this instance, our researcher has chosen a survey, and Designing Surveys includes steps on writing and organizing the questions, designing and selecting the sample, and tips on reducing sources of error in the collection.  Resources specific to data analysis and writing up your findings are also included.

asset.name: Designing Surveys: A Guide to Decisions and Procedures
asset.description: Access ebook through SAGE Research Methods.

asset.name: SAGE Research Methods Data Analysis Resources
asset.description: Access a variety of resources to support data analysis and interpretation.

asset.name: SAGE Research Methods Resources on Writing and Disseminating Your Research
asset.description: View resources, videos, and more on how to write up and disseminate your research findings.

9. Dissemination

Dissemination might be as simple as turning in your paper at the end of term. If you are completing a dissertation and/or looking to publish, SRM has information on that as well.

asset.name: Publishing Your Research
asset.description: Information on publishing your research from SAGE Research Methods.
Need to find a Method? Explore the Methods Map!

asset.name: Case Studies of real research projects
Streaming Video- see methods come to life
How the Brain Learns
asset.description: The human nerve center never rests—even during sleep, it works diligently to process and build on the information gathered by our senses. Of course, healthy sleep is only one of many vital ingredients the brain needs to develop and thrive, as this film illustrates in detail. Other factors discussed in the program include ongoing contact with negative (deterring) and positive (dopamine-triggering) stimuli, an environment that offers pattern repetition as well as deviation from repeating patterns as the brain emerges from infancy, and a sustained closeness between parent and child. Learning challenges such as dyslexia are also investigated, shedding further light on how our neural hub gains new skills, knowledge, and awareness. (30 minutes)
asset.author: Films for the Humanities & Sciences

asset.name: Is Seeing Believing? New Frontiers in the Science of the Senses
asset.description: From cooking breakfast to driving home from work, we rely on the body’s natural interfaces for nearly every task. Ironically, our senses are easily fooled and seem to affect each other in strange ways. This program follows new explorations in biology, neurology, and psychology that are shedding light on how the five senses work—not just as individual abilities but in tandem. Demonstrations feature bizarre optical illusions that reveal the subjectivity of color; a magic show that illuminates the eye-brain relationship; a synesthete who makes fresh food taste stale through the use of ambient sound; and a man who lost his sight as a child and has learned how to echolocate, bat-style, by clicking his tongue. Original BBC broadcast title: Is Seeing Believing? (60 minutes)
asset.author: Films for the Humanities & Sciences

asset.name: Never Enough: A Documentary
asset.description: "Do we own our things, or do they own us? Michele has 700 sweaters. When the pain of overcollecting outweighs the pleasure, she calls Ron "Disaster Master" Alford for help. Ron, a de-cluttering expert who believes "clutter begins in the head and ends up on the floor,' determines Michele is a hoarder with a rating of 8/10 on his 'clutter index.' Ron also visits a Marine with 7,800 Beanie Babies and a Home Shopping Network addict whose purchases are literally burying him. [This film] is a documentary meditation on materialism, consumerism, mental illness, and the social fabric of our lives." --
asset.author: Kelly Anderson

asset.name: Bipolar: Life Between Two Extremes
asset.description: Miami Airport, December 7, 2005: a jet passenger begins yelling about a bomb threat and bolts for the door. Refusing to comply with two U.S. marshals, he is eventually shot to death. The cause of his outburst—bipolar disorder, not terrorism—comes to light soon after, proffering another tragic example of how volatile and misunderstood the disease is. This program examines the lives of people who have struggled for decades with bipolar disorder, once known as manic depression. Through case studies and discussions of recent research, the film shows how each patient has overcome the grip of debilitating despair and hyperactive euphoria, and how advances in psychology and neuroscience are helping such individuals lead better, more productive lives. (45 minutes)
asset.author: Films for the Humanities & Sciences

asset.name: The Key of G
asset.description: The Key of G is an intimate, award-winning documentary about disability, caregiving, community integration and interdependence. The film follows Gannet, a charismatic 22-year-old with physical and developmental disabilities, as he leaves his mother's home to share an apartment with a group of artists and musicians who support him, not only as paid caregivers, but also as friends. Together they create a uniquely successful model of supported living, and a compelling alternative to institutionalized care.
asset.author: Co-production of Lateral Films and the Independent Television Service (ITVS)

asset.name: Prisoner of Her Past: Battling Late-Onset Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
asset.description: The haunting story of a secret childhood trauma resurfacing, sixty years later, to unravel the life of Holocaust survivor Sonia Reich. The film follows her son, Chicago Tribune jazz critic Howard Reich, as he journeys across the United States and Eastern Europe to uncover why his mother believes the world is conspiring to kill her. Along the way, he finds a family he never knew he had. This film is the first to illuminate a little-known illness: late-onset Post Traumatic Stress Disorder. This examines the disorder's devastating effect on families, but also shows programs that are aiding young trauma survivors of Hurricane Katrina, in New Orleans, and how such early interventions may have helped Howard's mother.
asset.author: Gordon Quinn, Jerry Blumenthal, Joanna Rudnick

asset.name: After Happily Ever After
asset.description: With half of American marriages ending in divorce, why does 90 percent of the nation still enter into matrimony? Is the Western notion of permanent, monogamous marriage entering a new phase, a more flexible and adaptable one, or is it becoming obsolete? Are there alternatives that make sense? This film presents an eclectic mix of couples (both male-female and same-sex) who discuss how and why their unions have succeeded, no matter how quirky, elusive, or poignant the reason. Featured experts include body-language analyst John Gottman, economist Betsey Stevenson, Beverly Hills divorce attorney Cary Goldstein, biologist David Barash, and marriage historian Stephanie Coontz. Along the way, the film’s director chronicles the joys and heartbreaks of her own marriage. Contains mature themes and nudity. (53 minutes)
asset.author: Films for the Humanities & Sciences

asset.name: Experimental Research Methods in Psychology
asset.description: Drawing upon laboratory and field experiments, this program compares and contrasts experimental research methods through an attractiveness study involving young adults. Section one observes how subjects respond to photos in two lab environments-one comfortable, and one not. Then, section two repeats the experiment in two field locales: a trendy bar and a dull coffee shop. Does context make a difference to the outcomes? The program concludes with a third section, in which experts explore some of the issues common to both experimental methods: demand characteristics, ethical concerns, and reductionism.

Find data

Start by thinking about who might care about, collect, or maintain the data. Depending on your topic, there might be government agencies, nongovernmental organizations, or industry research groups that collect and provide access to data. Review the library databases and freely available resources on this guide, consult a data repository index such as the Open Access Directory of Data Repositories, or try this formula in your preferred search engine: topic keywords + data + site:domain For example, if you were looking for reliable government data on gas prices, you might try: gas prices data site:.gov and find the U.S. Energy Information Administration page on weekly gas prices.

Manage data

Once you have found the data, you need to be sure you know how you will manage it. DataOne.org provides an excellent primer on data management and the data life cycle: plan, collect, assure, describe, preserve, and analyze.

Use data

Making sense of the data will often require knowledge of disciplinary research methods and statistical analysis. Sage Research Methods is a library resource that includes tools such as the Methods Map and Which Stats Test. Last but not least, remember to cite your data! The fine folks at Michigan State University Libraries have compiled a helpful guide for formatting citations to commonly used datasets and statistical tables in APA and MLA, and provides general principles for other styles.

asset.name: What's Next? : eco materialism & contemporary art
asset.description: By paying tribute to matter, materiality, and materialization, the examples of contemporary art assembled in What's Next? Eco Materialism and Contemporary Art challenge the social, cultural, and ethical norms that prevailed in the twentieth century. This significant frontier of contemporary culture is identified as 'Eco Materialism' because it affirms the emergent philosophy of Neo Materialism and attends to the pragmatic urgency of environmentalism.    In this highly original book, Linda Weintraub surveys the work of forty international artists who present materiality as a strategy to convert society's environmental neglect into responsible stewardship. These bold art initiatives, enriched by their associations with philosophy, ecology, and cultural critique, bear the hallmark of a significant new art movement. This accessible text, augmented with visuals, charts, and questionnaires, invites students and a wider readership to engage in this timely arena of contemporary art.
asset.author: Linda Weintraub

asset.name: William Wegman
asset.description: Fall in love with these funny, striking, and surreal pups. William Wegman's whimsical photographs of his Weimaraner dogs have been celebrated in the art world and enjoyed by pet lovers for nearly four decades. In this entirely new volume, renowned photography curator William A. Ewing presents more than 300 images from the artist's personal archive, unearthing previously unseen gems alongside the iconic images that have made Wegman--along with dressed-up dogs Man Ray, Fay Ray, and others--beloved worldwide. Presented in sixteen thematic chapters,William Wegman: Being Human foregrounds the photographer's penchant for play and his evergreen ability to create images that are at once funny, striking, and surreal. Audiences of all ages will fall in love--for the first time, or all over again--with Wegman and his friends.
asset.author: William A. Ewing; William Wegman (Photographer)

asset.name: Art and Reform in the Late Renaissance after Trent
asset.description: Drawing on recent research by established and emerging scholars of sixteenth- and seventeenth-century art, this volume reconsiders the art and architecture produced after 1563 across the conventional geographic borders. Rather than considering this period a degraded afterword to Renaissance classicism or an inchoate proto-Baroque, the book seeks to understand the art on its own terms. By considering artists such as Federico Barocci and Stefano Maderno in Italy, Hendrick Goltzius in the Netherlands, Antoine Caron in France, Francisco Ribalta in Spain, and Bartolomeo Bitti in Peru, the contributors highlight lesser known "reforms" of art from outside the conventional centers. As the first text to cover this formative period from an international perspective, this volume casts new light on the aftermath of the Renaissance and the beginnings of "Baroque."
asset.author: Jesse Locker

asset.name: The Artist As Curator
asset.description: Taking that ambiguous thing we call "the exhibition" as a critical medium, artists have often radically rethought conventional forms of exhibition making. The Artist as Curator: An Anthology, born out of a series of essays originally published in Mousse, surveys seminal examples of such artist-curated exhibitions from the postwar to the present, examined by the world's foremost curators and illustrated with rare documents and illustrations. Artists featured include the Avant-Garde Argentinian Visual Artists Group; Mel Bochner; Marcel Broothaers; John Cage; Judy Chicago, Miriam Schapiro and the CalArts Feminist Art Program; Collaborative Projects Inc. (Colab); Liam Gillick and Philippe Parreno; Group Material; Richard Hamilton and Victor Pasmore; David Hammons; Martin Kippenberger; Mark Leckey; H lio Oiticica; Walid Raad and Akram Zaatari; Martha Rosler; and Andy Warhol, among other examples drawn from around the globe.
asset.author: Elena Filipovic (Editor); Alexander Alberro; Monica Amor; Carlos Basualdo; Biljana Ciric

asset.name: Museum of Capitalism
asset.description: The Museum of Capitalism in Oakland, California, treats capitalism as a historical phenomenon. This speculative institution views the present and recent past from the implied perspective of a future society in which our economic and political system is memorialized, and subjected to the museological gaze. Sketches and renderings of exhibits and artifacts, combined with relevant quotations from historical sources, are interspersed with speculative essays on the intersections of ecology, race, museology, historiography, economics and politics. Included are representations of artworks and museum exhibits created by artists Oliver Ressler, Sayler/Morris, Dread Scott, Temporary Services, and others, original Isotype graphics drawn from the museum's lexicon of "capitalisms," and texts from Lucy Lippard, Lester K. Spence, T.J. Demos, Chantal Mouffe, McKenzie Wark and Kim Stanley Robinson, among others.
asset.author: Andrea Steves; Kim Robinson (Afterword by); T. J. Demos; Lucy R. Lippard; Chantal Mouffe; Mckenzie Wark

asset.name: The Dictionary of Art
asset.description: Boasting well over 6,000 contributors from 12 countries, the Dictionary offers its readers authoritative and comprehensive global coverage. A resource for both art and cultural studies, the Dictionary serves as a unique guide to all the visual arts: painting, sculpture, architecture, photography, drawing, printmaking, as well as the decorative arts. The Dictionary ranges far both geographically and historically; it features unparalleled coverage of Africa, Southeast Asia, Central Asia and Mongolia, China, India, the Islamic world, Japan, Korea, Native North America, Pacific and Aboriginal Australia, Pre-Columbian America, Ancient Egypt, Ancient Greece, the Ancient Near East, and Ancient Rome. Providing depth as well as breadth, The Dictionary of Art examines important art forms and key issues of design, taste, function, and patronage, illuminating them in light of the cultural context in which they developed.
asset.author: Jane Turner (Editor)

asset.name: Contemporary Artists
asset.description: 'Contemporary Artists' features comprehensive profiles of nearly 850 of the most significant artists woring in the contemporary era, with the vast majority of artists featured having produced their most significant work in the years after 1960.
asset.author: Sara Pendergast (Editor); Tom Pendergast (Editor)

asset.name: Encyclopedia of 20th-Century Architecture
asset.description: For more information including the introduction, a full list of entries and contributors, a generous selection of sample pages and more, visit the Encyclopedia of 20th Century Architecturewebsite. Focusing on architecture from all regions of the world, this three-volume set profiles the twentieth century's vast chronicle of architectural achievements, both within and well beyond the theoretical confines of modernism. Unlike existing works, this encyclopedia examines the complexities of rapidly changing global conditions that have dispersed modern architectural types, movements, styles, and building practices across traditional geographic and cultural boundaries.
asset.author: R. Stephen Sennott (Editor)

asset.name: The Grove Encyclopedia of Classical Art and Architecture
asset.description: The Grove Encyclopedia of Classical Art and Architecture spans every art form, medium, and civilization the fall of the Roman Empire, The Grove Encyclopedia of Classical Art & Architecture is a comprehensive reference source on this important field of study. Drawing on the expansive scholarship of The Dictionary of Art (1996, 34 vols) and Grove Art Online, and adding dozens of new entries, the Encyclopedia includes all subject areas in the classical arts, including philosophers, rulers, writers and artists, architecture, ceramics, sculpture, and more. Arranged alphabetically, this two-volume set contains over 800 entries tracing the development of the art forms in classical civilizations such as ancient Greece and Rome. Illustrated with 400 halftones, maps and line drawings, and 32 color plates, the Encyclopedia is a reliable and convenient resource covering this field of everlasting significance in the development of western culture.
asset.author: Gordon Campbell

asset.description: A collection of essays by Paul Bennet and others, including a bibliography illustrated with photographs. It also contains the earliest recorded account of the group's history. Initiated by Bennett in the early 1930s, the Typophiles met weekly to discuss their shared passion for printing, typography, and the graphic arts.

asset.name: Emma Bell Miles Southern Appalachia art and correspondence
asset.description: The Emma Bell Miles Southern Appalachia art and correspondence digital collection contains correspondence among members and friends of writer and artist Emma Bell Miles’ family of origin illustrating the personal roots of themes Emma lived out and developed in her work. The heart of the collection is a series of letters written during 1901-1903 concerning Emma’s troubled relationship with her parents, her life as a young woman, and her life as an emerging artist and naturalist; as well as the death of her mother, Emma’s marriage to Frank Miles soon thereafter, and disposition of Bell family property in Walden Ridge, Tennessee. The collection also features numerous examples of Emma's art, including watercolors, oil paintings, and sketches.
asset.author: Miles, Emma Bell, 1879-1919
